source.quote: Rotel's own page for the S14, read 2026-11-25. « Coax/Optical Digital Input Signals » / « SPDIF LPCM (Up to 24-bit/192kHz) ». « PC-USB » / « USB Audio Class 2.0 (up to 24-bit/384kHz)* ». « MQA and MQA Studio (up to 24-bit/384kHz ) ». Flash drive: « plays MP3, WMA and AAC files from flash drives », with no rate. DAC: « ESS premium 32-bit Digital to Analog Converter » (feature icon) and « 32-bit ESS DAC » (description). No DSD row and no digital filter row.

facts.chip: « ESS premium 32-bit Digital to Analog Converter » - the family and a word length, no part number.

_verification_des_conditions_tentee: No terms page is linked from rotel.com's home page, its product listing or the product pages read; the footer offers Contact Us, a Privacy Policy and « (c) Grand Green Limited ». The privacy policy WAS read and covers registrations, mailing lists and analytics, with no clause on using or reproducing site content. No URL was guessed, so a terms page elsewhere on the site is not ruled out.
_le_convertisseur_est_32_bits_et_lentree: « ESS premium 32-bit Digital to Analog Converter » against « USB Audio Class 2.0 (up to 24-bit/384kHz) ». bits is 24, because the field means what the device accepts and the USB row is the statement about that; the 32 describes the silicon. The RA-1592MKII and the A14MKII, same maker, both accept 32 bits over Class 2 - so this is a property of this model's receiver, not a house convention.
